cells.tense: You're moving toward what you want right now, and it isn't costing you anything to keep going.
cells.verb: wanting and doing pointing the same way, at a pace you can hold
cells.place: where you keep the balance by small corrections as you go
cells.ask: Let yourself picture where this pace could actually arrive — all the way, not the modest version — and see what deep satisfaction in a thing you imagined feels like.
cells.core: You're moving toward what you want right now, and it isn't costing you anything to keep going. The wanting and the doing are pointed the same way, and you're adjusting as you go — a little more here, a little less there — without it ever turning into a fight. Effort feels like effort is supposed to feel. That's not a finish line; it's a steady engine with fuel to spare. If you're willing, let yourself picture where this pace could actually arrive — all the way, not the modest version — and see what deep satisfaction in a thing you imagined feels like.
cells.sheetLine: You're going where you want at a pace you can hold. Picture where it could arrive.

cells.tense: You're going to keep the rhythm going no matter what, and you're already tightening against the moment it might slip.
cells.verb: keeping the drive steady by never letting it rest
cells.place: where you keep the balance by small corrections as you go
cells.ask: Stop and gather it once — sit with everything in play until it's one picture instead of a hundred nudges — and notice how the going starts coming from what you actually want again.
cells.core: You're going to keep the rhythm going no matter what, and you're already tightening against the moment it might slip. So you correct constantly — a nudge here, a push there, never letting the pace settle for fear it won't come back. The adjusting has stopped serving the movement and started replacing it. Steadiness doesn't survive being guarded that hard. If you're willing, stop and gather it once — sit with everything in play until it's one picture instead of a hundred nudges — and notice how the going starts coming from what you actually want again.
cells.sheetLine: You're correcting the pace so hard there's no pace left. Gather it into one picture.

lint.detail: the tense sentence does not read as Too Much's time

cells.tense: You had a rhythm once, and you're still waiting at the spot where it went quiet.
cells.verb: letting the drive idle instead of pointing it anywhere
cells.place: where you keep the balance by small corrections as you go
cells.ask: Take stock of what the last change actually grew — name what's in your hands now that wasn't before — and let direction come back from what you really feel about it.
cells.core: You had a rhythm once, and you're still waiting at the spot where it went quiet. The wanting is in there; it just isn't moving anything, and the small adjustments that used to keep things flowing have stopped altogether. You're not fighting the current. You've stepped out of it. Pushing harder won't start it — that's the one thing that won't. If you're willing, take stock of what the last change actually grew — name what's in your hands now that wasn't before — and let direction come back from what you really feel about it.
cells.sheetLine: The rhythm went quiet and you're still standing where it stopped. Count what the change grew.

cells.tense: You're already moving steadily toward something, adjusting as you go, and you're calling it circumstance.
cells.verb: steering the drive without claiming you're steering it
cells.place: where you keep the balance by small corrections as you go
cells.ask: Pick one thing you keep showing up for and call it yours — built, not happened — and feel how the direction starts coming from what you genuinely want.
cells.core: You're already moving steadily toward something, adjusting as you go, and you're calling it circumstance. Things happen to line up, you'd say — the days just go this way. But the pace is yours, and so are the hundred small corrections that keep it. The steering is running. The hand on it is unsigned. If you're willing, pick one thing you keep showing up for and call it yours — built, not happened — and feel how the direction starts coming from what you genuinely want.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this already. You just call it how things turned out.
